messages:
neha: POC update — Acme Health says the patient-summary streaming endpoint keeps dropping mid-response. They see SSE disconnects and JSON.parse failures on the client. Need a quick swarming session, this is blocking the demo tomorrow
anna: Client logs: 
`Error: Unexpected end of JSON input`
And they pasted this fragment from their side:
```
data: {"id":"p-123","name":"John Doe","summary":"History: HTN, DM
data: {"id":"p-124","name":"Jane"  <-- gets cutoff and then connection closes
```
anna: They said it happens after ~25-40s of streaming, usually when we flush larger chunks
dmitri: Thanks. Two quick suspects: (1) server-side flush boundaries causing partial JSON to be delivered before a full record, (2) an intermediate proxy/firewall closing idle streaming connections. Do we have the server-side access logs and any nginx/proxy upstream errors?
sam: Can you grab the proxy/gateway logs and the app logs around a failing session id? Also, what client library are they using — plain EventSource or a custom SSE client?
anna: They're using a React app with EventSource polyfill. I'll grab logs.
anna: App proxy log (excerpt):
```
[2026-02-12T14:07:02.123Z] GET /v1/stream/patient-summary 200  (chunked)
[2026-02-12T14:07:31.987Z] upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.x.x.x, server: api.redwood, request: "GET /v1/stream/patient-summary", upstream: "http://10.2.3.4:8080/", host: "api.acme.example"
```
dmitri: That upstream message is telling — either the app crashed or the app closed the socket mid-stream. Can we see the app stdout? Also check if there's an idle timeout from a frontend LB (30s default sometimes).
anna: App stdout shows repeated flushes of events and then this trace when it closes:
```
streamer: flush 8192 bytes id=p-123
streamer: flush 4096 bytes id=p-123
Error: write EPIPE
    at afterWriteDispatched (internal/stream_base_commons.js:...)
```
sam: EPIPE suggests the client closed the connection first (or a proxy did). Two-pronged fix: (A) make SSE payloads self-contained per event (send a full JSON per event, not split across flushes), and (B) add periodic heartbeat/ping events to keep proxies from timing out.
dmitri: Also check TLS offloading/proxy; many corporate firewalls will silently drop long-lived connections. Recommend heartbeat < 20s for enterprise customers.
neha: Any quick client-side workaround we can suggest so the React EventSource doesn't crash parsing partial JSON?
sam: Yes — EventSource should treat each SSE "data:" event as a complete message. If you're streaming a large JSON that itself contains newlines, split it as multiple data: lines per event or base64-encode the payload. But simpler: stream newline-delimited JSON objects and parse only when you see a full object (e.g., buffer until you detect `\n\n` separator). Here's a tiny client pattern: 
```
// pseudo
let buf = '';
es.addEventListener('message', e => {
  buf += e.data;
  if (buf.endsWith('\n')) {
    try { const obj = JSON.parse(buf.trim()); handle(obj); }
    catch(e){ /* wait for more */ }
    buf = '';
  }
});
```
sam: On the server side, two config knobs we recommended to Acme for the POC: set the SSE heartbeat to 15s and flush smaller, complete events (or disable mid-event flush). In the POC config we can add: 
```
streaming: true
sse_heartbeat_ms: 15000
sse_chunking: complete_event
```
anna: Also worth noting — Acme's security/compliance team flagged long-lived sockets as an enterprise blocker. They asked if we can guarantee encrypted and proxied connections remain open and that logs are audit-friendly. I raised this with SEC but wanted to call it out here.
dmitri: For production we usually recommend Dedicated capacity for enterprise customers — it reduces the number of intermediate proxies and gives predictable network paths. For the POC we can push the heartbeat + complete-event flush to unblock the demo.
deploy-bot: canary: deployed rev a3f9 -> enable sse_heartbeat_ms=15000 on canary streaming pool (10:58)
anna: I asked the client to try the canary URL and lower their EventSource reconnection backoff. They tested and reported: "no parse errors for 45m, connection stayed open, events now come as discrete JSON objects"
neha: Great — does this fully remove the enterprise blocker or do we still have the security questionnaire outstanding?
anna: They still want confirmation about audit log retention and KMS keys for PII in transit/storage. I put that to SEC and will follow up separately. For the immediate demo, the streaming stability blocker is resolved.
dmitri: Followups: (1) capture long-run smoke test for 24h on canary, (2) add automated SSE heartbeat metric/alert if clients reconnect > X% in window, (3) doc snippet for customers showing recommended SSE best-practices (heartbeat, per-event JSON, backoff).
neha: Thanks team — I'll update the ACME success plan and move this POC to 'ready for demo'. :tada:
anna: Confirmed demo tomorrow at 10am PT.
deploy-bot: monitor: streaming-pool-canary healthy (last 5m no reconnections spike)"
